conviction_note: The quarter is a book-value collapse the market already knows about. Q3 2026 saw the 10y up about 87bp to 5.29%, agency MBS -3.3% total and -1.0% excess in September, and same-leverage peers ORC and IVR pre-released Q3 book declines of about 16%. DX at $10.91 is already about 0.97x a peer-implied ~$11.27 Sept-30 book. The 2023 analogue (DX TER -11% against ORC -15.8%) gives DX a mild relative-hedging plus on the Sept-30 number. That is roughly offset by an October quarter-to-date update likely to be negative (30y mortgage rate 7.28% to 7.40%, AGNC -3.6% since Sept 30; in the Oct-2023 analogue DX fell 3.5% on the print). So p_up 48 on an abs move of 2.5%. That is larger than the 0.81% calm-quarter median because stressed quarters move this name more.
bar: There is no sourced consensus for Q3 book value, the line this name trades on, so every size is capped small. Working bar: a peer-implied Sept-30 book of about $11.27, from June book $12.90 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000074/a2q26earningsrelease.htm) with ORC's Q3 TER of -12.5% scaled by DX/ORC's Q3-2023 TER ratio (DX -11.0%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667523000095/a3q23earningsrelease.htm; ORC -15.77%, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231026165984/en/Orchid-Island-Capital-Announces-Third-Quarter-2023-Results) and $0.51 of dividends taken off. EPS/EAD consensus is $0.37 on one source only (Google Finance snippet; Q2 EAD was $0.36). Sell-side targets were cut in early October, KBW $15 to $12.50 and BTIG $14.50 to $12 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dx/), so the analysts have already marked book down.
positioning_check: Short interest 17.5m shares, 7.14% of float, 2.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30, up 6.0% from 09-15 (MarketBeat via sweep, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/DX/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. No usable skew: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid), ATM IV 35.4% against 23.9% 20d realised, put/call OI 1.09. Spot $10.91 is 3% above the 52w low, -10.4% over 20d and about -17% since the 6/30 close of $13.09. The sector moved with it: AGNC 10.90 to 8.74, and ORC trades at 0.82x its own pre-released book.

findings.finding: Two agency mREITs at DX-like leverage have already pre-released Q3 2026 books down about 16%: ORC $7.22 to $6.02 (-16.6%, est. GAAP loss $0.90/sh, TER about -12.5%, 8-K 2026-10-14) and IVR $8.03 to $6.74 (-16.1%; $7.74 at Aug 31, so most of the loss came in September). In Q3 2023, the closest analogue (a 10y spike plus a Fed hike), DX's TER was -11.0% against ORC's -15.8%, a ratio of 0.70. Applied here that gives DX a Sept-30 book of about $11.27 (-12.6%), and at $10.91 the stock trades at about 0.97x it, against about 1.01x at June 30. The likely Sept-30 print is bad in absolute terms but in line with or slightly better than what the price already discounts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Book value is the line. In calm quarters, close-to-close reactions were small: Q2 2026 -1.58% (7/17 13.33 to 7/20 13.12) and Q1 2026 +0.81% (13.61 to 13.72), both verified on Yahoo bars, so the baseline's numbers ARE the right close-to-close window despite the 'intraday' label. In the stressed Q3 2023 print (book -13.7%), DX fell 3.5% close-to-close (10/20/2023 10.67 to 10/23 10.30, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DX?period1=1697673600&period2=1698278400&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: The absolute book decline IS priced: DX is down about 17% since June 30 and ORC barely moved on its pre-release (5.06 to 5.08). What may not be priced is DX's relative hedge outperformance. If the market expected DX's book to fall as much as ORC/IVR (about -16%, to about $10.84), DX would already trade at about 1.0x that, which it does. So the price looks consistent with a peer-like -15 to -16% book, and a -12 to -13% print would be a small relative beat.
findings.independence: IVR 8-K, a separate document from a different company, points the same way: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000076/ivr10142026-8kxex991.htm (Sept 30 $6.74) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000051/ivr07152026-8kxex991.htm (June 30 $8.03). The macro series agree: BofA agency MBS September -3.3% total / -1.0% excess (https://finvaulta.com/research/bank-of-america/securitized-products-returns-for-september-2026-2026-10-02). The relative-hedging part rests only on the 2023 DX/ORC ratio, which is an inference.

findings.finding: Agency conditions kept deteriorating after quarter end. The Freddie Mac 30y rate went 7.03% (9/24) to 7.28% (10/1) to 7.40% (10/8), and held 7.40% on 10/15, the eighth week without a decline. AGNC fell 9.07 to 8.74 (-3.6%) from 9/30 to 10/16. DX gives a quarter-to-date book on its call (on the Q2 call it gave book as of July 17, $12.67), so the 10:00 ET call will likely add an October QTD decline on top of the Sept-30 number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no formal guide. The QTD book update is the forward line. In Oct 2023, with rates still rising into the print, DX fell 3.5% on the day. In Q2 2026 a softer QTD book ($12.67 against $12.90 at quarter end) came with a -1.58% reaction.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-01 (with the 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-15 items on the same page)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: DX is down 2.2% since 9/30 (11.14 to 10.91) before its October ex-dividend date (Oct 22). With no usable option chain and a 0.81% calm-quarter median, the name has no visible event premium for a negative QTD surprise. The QTD book number itself has not been disclosed anywhere.
findings.independence: AGNC price series (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/AGNC?range=6mo&interval=1d) and Q2-call QTD disclosure precedent via stockanalysis (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dx/). Macro-to-company transmission is not confirmed by DX itself, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: The CIO, Terrence Connelly Jr., bought 2,500 DX shares in the open market at $11.18 on 2026-09-25 (code P, about $28k, holding 58,695 afterwards), five sessions before quarter end, while the stock traded at about 0.87x the June book. Insiders' only other September Form 4s were tax-withholding F codes at $12.89.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of insider-buy signals moving this name's prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a small purchase on EDGAR that nobody aggregates for an $2.6bn mREIT, and the stock fell a further 2.4% after it. If the market read it as a book-value signal, DX would not trade at the bottom of the peer P/B range. It is weak, because the dollar size is token.

findings.finding: DX priced $120m of 9.375% Series D cumulative preferred (4.8m shares) on 2026-09-22 rather than issuing common below book. Use of proceeds is buying Agency securities, at current-coupon spreads of about 120bp (BofA), wider than the 107bp at June 30 (DoubleLine). That is accretive to common if levered ROE on new purchases exceeds 9.375%, but it adds senior capital and leverage to the common.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior preferred issuance near a print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since the stock fell 3.1% on 9/23-9/24 alongside the sector. What the call adds is how much was deployed and at what spread, and whether leverage rose or fell.
findings.independence: Spread levels come from different sources: https://finvaulta.com/research/bank-of-america/securitized-products-returns-for-september-2026-2026-10-02 and DoubleLine Q2 (https://doubleline.com/markets-insights/securitized-products-briefing/).

findings.finding: Earnings available for distribution of $0.36 in Q2 covered only about 70% of the $0.51 quarterly dividend ($0.17 monthly, held for October on 2026-10-12). The Fed's 25bp hike on 2026-09-16 raised repo costs for the last two weeks of Q3, and the swaps that receive floating offset only part of that. A soft EAD against the $0.37 single-source consensus would sharpen the coverage question on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EAD rose 0.31 to 0.36 in Q2 and the stock still fell 1.58%. EAD has not been the line this name reacts to.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage below the dividend has been public for quarters, and the October dividend was just held. The only new piece is the hike's effect on funding cost. The bar is one source, so this is capped.
findings.independence: October dividend held: https://finviz.com/news/401422/dynex-capital-inc-declares-october-monthly-common-stock-dividend-of-017 (which cuts against a dividend-cut reading inside the window).

outside_window.finding: AGNC (usually the Monday after the close) and Annaly report Q3 after DX. Their book updates and QTD commentary land after the 2026-10-19 close or later, so they sit outside DX's window.
Possible dividend reset given EAD coverage of about 70%. The next monthly declaration is mid-November.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The -10.4% 20d run-up and a price near the 52w low already embed the sector-wide Q3 book collapse that peers have pre-released, so the evidence mostly says 'priced', with offsetting small edges.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (the bar has one source or none): there is no book consensus and the EAD consensus has one source, so the EAD finding was capped from -0.3 to -0.2 and the cap is stated in `bar`.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company is a proxy): the October QTD finding rests on mortgage rates and AGNC's price, not a DX document, so it was cut from -0.8 to -0.6. It is still filed.

Rebuild an untrustworthy history: two prior bmo prints were checked against Yahoo daily bars and the baseline numbers are the correct close-to-close window. I added the Q3-2023 stressed print (-3.5%) to set abs_move at 2.5 rather than the 0.81 median.
Rule 4 (financing): asked what the Series D buys (agency assets at wider spreads). Signed small positive, unchanged.
Rule 7 (positioning): 7.14% of float short, 2.2 days to cover, not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk further for squeeze risk.
